title: Soundness of the inner-language condition
statement: Let $d$ be a refutation data package and let $L_2,K$ be languages of Boolean strings. Suppose that for every string $y$, membership in $L_2$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $v$ with $|v|=M_2(y)$ and $\langle y,v\rangle\in K$. Suppose that for every string $z$, nonmembership in $K$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $r$ with $|r|\le C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ and $\langle z,r\rangle\in R$. Assume that for all Boolean strings $x,U,u,v,w,r$ with $|u|=M_1(x)$, $|v|\le M_2(\langle x,u\rangle)$, $|w|\le|U|$, and $|r|\le C_3(nLen(x)+1)^{c_3}$, one has $|\langle\langle u,v\rangle,\langle w,r\rangle\rangle|\le B(|\langle x,U\rangle|+1)^b$. If $\langle x,U\rangle$ belongs to the inner language and $|u|=M_1(x)$, then $\langle x,u\rangle\in L_2$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $y$, $y\in L_2$ iff there exists $v$ with $|v|=M_2(y)$ and $\langle y,v\rangle\in K$
For every $z$, $z\notin K$ iff there exists $r$ with $|r|\le C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ and $\langle z,r\rangle\in R$
The stated length bound holds for all $x,U,u,v,w,r$ satisfying the four listed length constraints
$\langle x,U\rangle$ belongs to the inner language
replaced:
Let $d$ be data, and let $L_2,K,R$ be languages of bit strings. Suppose that for every
bit string $y$, membership in $L_2$ is equivalent to the existence of a bit string $v$
of length $M_2(y)$ for which the encoding of $(y,v)$ belongs to $K$. Suppose also that
for every $z$, nonmembership of $z$ in $K$ is equivalent to the existence of a bit
string $r$ with $|r|\le C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ whose pairing with $z$ belongs to $R$. Assume
that for all bit strings $x,U,u,v,w,r$ with $|u|=M_1(x)$, $|v|\le M_2(\langle
x,u\rangle)$, $|w|\le |U|$, and $|r|\le C_3(nLen(x)+1)^{c_3}$, the length of
$\langle\langle u,v\rangle,\langle w,r\rangle\rangle$ is at most $B(|\langle
x,U\rangle|+1)^b$. If $\langle x,U\rangle$ belongs to the inner language and
$|u|=M_1(x)$, then $\langle x,u\rangle\in L_2$.
